landmarks.name: Red Fort
landmarks.hint: A UNESCO World Heritage red sandstone fort, the seat of Mughal power, where India's PM addresses the nation on Independence Day

landmarks.name: India Gate
landmarks.hint: A war memorial on Rajpath, dedicated to soldiers who died in World War I, with the eternal Amar Jawan Jyoti flame

landmarks.name: Qutb Minar
landmarks.hint: A UNESCO World Heritage minaret and victory tower, the tallest brick minaret in the world, built in 1193

landmarks.name: Humayun's Tomb
landmarks.hint: The first garden-tomb on the Indian subcontinent, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and precursor to the Taj Mahal

landmarks.name: Lotus Temple
landmarks.hint: A Bahá'í House of Worship shaped like a blooming lotus flower, open to people of all faiths

landmarks.name: Akshardham Temple
landmarks.hint: A massive Hindu temple complex on the Yamuna bank, with intricate pink sandstone carvings and water shows

landmarks.name: Jama Masjid
landmarks.hint: India's largest mosque, built by Shah Jahan, with three marble domes and two minarets in Old Delhi

landmarks.name: Rashtrapati Bhavan
landmarks.hint: The official residence of the President of India, a vast colonial and Mughal-inspired building on Raisina Hill

landmarks.name: Connaught Place
landmarks.hint: The financial and commercial heart of New Delhi, a colonnaded circular plaza designed by Robert Tor Russell

landmarks.name: Chandni Chowk
landmarks.hint: One of the oldest and busiest markets in Old Delhi, a labyrinth of narrow lanes with food stalls and shops
